one_line: Clean up how a customer's push registration is stored so dead ones are removed and one device holds one, and then tell the marketing system which customers can actually be reached by push so a campaign can fall back to email.
questions: Should a customer count as unreachable as soon as one delivery fails, or only after we have failed to reach them several times?
When a customer turns notifications back on, how quickly does the marketing system need to know - immediately, or is the next daily sync soon enough?
If the sync to the marketing system is down, should a campaign hold and wait or go out using the last reachability we knew about?

split_into.title: Clean up rejected and duplicate push registrations
split_into.description: Remove push registrations the provider has rejected, and keep one registration per device.

split_into.title: Share push reachability with the marketing system
split_into.description: Tell the marketing system which customers can be reached by push, so a campaign can fall back to email when they cannot.

acceptance_criteria: A push registration the provider rejects is removed rather than retried forever.
One device holds one push registration.
A registration that has gone unused past a defined age is expired.
Whether a customer can be reached by push is available to the marketing system as a property of that customer.
A campaign can use that property to send email instead of push.
not_verified: The ticket says the first half has already landed, and I could not confirm that from what I was able to read - so it is worth checking before anybody starts, because the two halves have different owners. Nothing we have written down says how many failed deliveries mean a customer is unreachable, or how fresh the marketing system needs that answer to be, and both of those change what gets built rather than only how.
notes: The two halves are better tracked separately: the first is cleanup with no visible effect on customers, the second changes what a campaign does and can be got wrong in a way people notice. The ticket says the first half is done, which if true makes this really only the second half - worth confirming with the team rather than assuming either way. The failure question matters most: treating one failed delivery as unreachable would quietly move customers to email who could have been reached.
